findings.title: New concurrency test never requests sub-group counts, so it does not exercise the fixed method
findings.body: The reader thread calls `groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)`. The fourth parameter of that admin-client overload is `briefRepresentation` (see `getGroupsWithBriefAndFullRepresentation` in the same file, where `false` yields full attributes), so the `subGroupsCount` query parameter is not sent and defaults to `false` on the server. `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()` (the method changed in this PR) is only invoked via `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount`, which is guarded by `if (subGroupsCount)`. As written, this test never calls the fixed method and would pass with the fix reverted, so it provides no protection against the NPE it is meant to cover. The read must request sub-group counts (e.g. the overload that passes `subGroupsCount=true`) or otherwise force `getSubGroupsCount()` to run while the groups are being deleted.

findings.title: Reader thread is never joined, so the assertion races with it and can pass vacuously
findings.body: `new Thread(...).start()` is fire-and-forget: after the deletes, `deletedAll.set(true)` is followed immediately by `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())`. The assertion can run before the worker has completed (or even started) a single list request, so the test passes without exercising the concurrent read at all, and an exception thrown by an in-flight request after the assertion is silently lost. In addition, if any `remove()` throws, `deletedAll` is never set and the non-daemon worker keeps calling the admin client during and after realm teardown. Set the flag in a `finally` block, `join(timeout)` the worker before asserting, and fail if the thread did not run at least one read iteration.

findings.title: Same NPE still present in the getSubGroupsStream(search/exact, first, max) overloads
findings.body: The fix guards `modelSupplier.get()` against null only in `getSubGroupsCount()`. The three overloads at lines 256, 262 and 268 still do `return modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` directly. `modelSupplier` resolves to `cacheSession.getGroupDelegate().getGroupById(realm, cached.getId())`, which returns `null` when the group is removed concurrently - exactly the condition this PR fixes for the count. A request for subgroups with search/paging on a concurrently deleted group therefore still throws an NPE and returns a 500. The same null handling should be applied here (e.g. return `Stream.empty()` when the delegate is gone).
